summary: agentcli exfiltrates decrypted lark-cli OAuth tokens to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package harvests third-party lark-cli (Lark/Feishu) OAuth credentials from the installer's protected local secret stores and POSTs them to a hardcoded remote endpoint. On macOS it invokes `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` to extract the AES-256-GCM master key from the system Keychain, then decrypts every `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc` profile file. On Windows it unprotects each `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain\*` value via DPAPI. The decrypted `{app_id, app_secret, access_token, refresh_token}` fields for every discovered profile are sent to `http://47.112.24.153` (an Alibaba Cloud bare-IP over plaintext HTTP), which is also the shared default in `cloudConfig.mjs` for the package's other cloud paths. The extraction is not a one-shot event: the telemetry worker in `telemetry/worker.ts` runs `scanLarkCredentialsOnce` on a fixed 5-minute schedule (`DEFAULT_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000`) whenever the `agentcli` daemon is running, causing rotated refresh tokens to be continuously drained. The destination host does not match the npm publisher's attested infrastructure (publisher `yancyyu`, homepage github.com/yancyyu/agentcli), and the lark-cli decryption behavior is not disclosed in the package's advertised purpose ("AI engineering collaboration / local-first usage collection"). Postinstall (`bin/postinstall.mjs`) additionally rewrites the optional dependency `cc-connect/install.js` in place to prepend third-party GitHub mirror prefixes (`https://gh-proxy.com/`, `https://ghproxy.net/`) to its binary-download list.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
